classification.difficultyReason: Combine semicircle and centre–circumference angle properties with an equilateral triangle, then use Pythagoras to find an exact length.

content.prompt: In the circle with centre $O$, $AB$ is a diameter and $BC=OB$.

spec.description: Unshaded circle with horizontal diameter AB, centre O, D above C on a vertical chord, and segments AC and DB. BC and OC are not drawn. Decorative blue strokes and the red centre marker are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: A, B, C and D lie on the circle; AB is a diameter; BC equals the radius OB. C and D lie at the lower-right and upper-right respectively.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source-supplied geometry and labels are visible; no calculated angles, added radii or solution lengths.

answer.worked:
$$\angle ACB=90^\circ$$
An angle in a semicircle is a right angle because $AB$ is a diameter.

Join $OC$ and $BC$. Since $OB=OC$ are radii and $BC=OB$, triangle $BOC$ is equilateral.
$$\angle BOC=60^\circ$$

The angle at the circumference standing on arc $BC$ is half the angle at the centre standing on that arc.
$$\begin{align*}\angle CAB&=\tfrac12\angle BOC\\\angle CAB&=\tfrac12\times60^\circ\\\angle CAB&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$

The angle at the circumference standing on arc $CB$ is half the angle at the centre standing on that arc.
$$\begin{align*}\angle CDB&=\tfrac12\angle COB\\\angle CDB&=\tfrac12\times60^\circ\\\angle CDB&=30^\circ\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the radius of the circle is $6\text{ cm}$, find $AC$.

answer.worked:
$AB=12\text{ cm}$ and $BC=6\text{ cm}$. Since $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, use Pythagoras’ theorem:
$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=AB^2-BC^2\\AC^2&=12^2-6^2\\AC^2&=108\\AC&=\sqrt{108}\\AC&=6\sqrt3\text{ cm}.\end{align*}$$
